messages:
inc-bot: STATUS: Partial customer impact in hosted inference (us-central) — increased 5xxs and tail latency for requests using streaming + long-context (>4k). Impact window started ~13:12 UTC. Live incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1715098765 :rotating_light:

sam: Observed surge of retries on the streaming muxer causing connection throttling. p99 for streaming sessions jumped from ~600ms -> ~3.2s. Sample error from muxer:
```
ERR muxer: write timeout after 45s, client=172.18.9.4
WARN stream-proxy: upstream reset during chunked response
```

nina: I see correlated growth in stream-buffer memory and many long-lived sessions pinning kernel resources. Looks like a queue compaction/regression in the stream scheduler. Rolling back recent stream-scheduler change on canary now.

tal: initiating rollback: `platform deploy --service stream-scheduler --region us-central --version v2026-03-18 --subset canary`

ops: mitigation actions applied:
- paused stream-scheduler rollout (v2026-03-19)
- rolled back 20% canary -> v2026-03-18
- temporarily increased streaming pool autoscale headroom by +25%
- applied per-session idle eviction at 90s to free kernel resources for long sessions
- enabled model-size fallback for customers on >8k contexts (suggested fallback to smaller-context variant)

support: drafting customer notice: "We detected intermittent streaming failures and elevated latency for long-context requests in us-central. We have applied a rollback and mitigations; engineers are monitoring. More info: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1715098765" Planning to send to affected tenants in 7 minutes.

sam: canary rollback shows improvement: error rate on canary hosts down ~85% within 90s. p99 trending back toward baseline. Expanding rollback to 60% while monitoring.

alerts: Grafana links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streams/streaming-overview?from=now-30m&to=now and streaming-muxer trace: https://traces.redwood.example/trace/1715098765

nina: collecting heap profiles and scheduler traces from affected hosts to /incidents/1715098765/artifacts. Please avoid recycling hosts until we capture them.

tal: running a constrained reintroduce plan if stable for 15m: reintroduce at 10% with lowered concurrency cap and extra logging. Command for controlled reintroduce: `platform deploy --service stream-scheduler --version v2026-03-19 --region us-central --percent 10 --concurrency-cap 8`

ops: customer impact details: ~3-6% of hosted streaming requests affected, primarily customers with long-context, streaming sessions. No data exfiltration observed. Tagged enterprise tenants for direct outreach.

support: standing by for replies. Sending staged broadcast to #customers-facing in 7m if metrics remain stable.

sam: action items (post-incident):
- add regression test for stream-scheduler under high long-lived session loads (ENG-9912)
- add automatic rollback trigger when streaming muxer error rate >0.5% for 2m (OPS-1147)
- investigate queue compaction change that landed in v2026-03-19

nina: note: also plan to add a safe default that caps per-session kernel allocation for streaming contexts >4k so one session can't starve others.

inc-bot: Incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1715098765 (runbook + artifacts). Broadcast scheduled to customers in ~7m pending stability.

ops: monitoring: p95/p99 and error-rate graphs returning to baseline on rolled-back nodes. Will keep incident open for 30m post-stability and then send final customer update. :white_check_mark:

support: final note before close: if anyone sees a recurrence, tag `@oncall` immediately and attach traces to the incident artifacts.
